subject: Baldwin SIG: questions on prompt/log lifecycle, training usage, and retention options
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@baldwinhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@baldwinhealth.com
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG Section C - clarifications on prompt logs and training usage

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We're working through the SIG Section C questions and have a few follow-ups specific to how Redwood treats customer prompts and inference logs: 
- How long are raw prompts and model responses retained in hosted Redwood by default?
- Are prompts/response logs ever used to train or improve Redwood models or third-party models? If yes, under what agreements?
- Can customers configure no-retention or immediate redaction for their tenant?
- Do backups, snapshots, or long-term archives ever contain prompt/response content?

I've attached our trimmed Section C worksheet (Baldwin_SIG_SectionC.xlsx) with the rows we're stuck on. Can you point us to an evidence packet or short statements we can include in the SIG?

We appreciate a short written response we can include in our security team review; if easier, we'll set up a 20-minute call.

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Senior Procurement Manager
Baldwin Health

(attachment: Baldwin_SIG_SectionC.xlsx)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@baldwinhealth.com>, procurement@baldwinhealth.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG Section C - clarifications on prompt logs and training usage

Sarah — thanks for the clear list and the worksheet. High-level answers below; I included Monica (Security) and Priyom (Product) in case you want more technical evidence or a quick call. I'll attach a compact evidence packet and a retention matrix.

Short answers (hosted Redwood API):
- Default retention: ephemeral operational logs (request/response traces used for troubleshooting) are retained for 30 days by default. Aggregated metrics and anonymized telemetry used for product health are retained longer per our retention matrix (attached).
- Training usage: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts or model outputs for training or improving base models by default. Customer content will only be used for model training if explicitly agreed in contract (opt-in) and processed under a documented data handling workflow.
- No-retention/opt-out: For Hosted customers, we offer a "no-logging" or "no-training" flag at the tenant level that suppresses storing request/response payloads beyond immediate processing; this must be enabled at account setup or through your customer success rep. For Dedicated deployments, retention can be configured per-customer and limited to zero in many cases. For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), all logs remain under customer control.
- Backups/snapshots: Persistent backups for the control plane (metadata, billing) do not include raw prompt/response payloads. Operational traces that contain payloads are excluded from long-term backups by default; short-term troubleshooting snapshots may include them but are time-limited and access-controlled.

I've attached a short evidence PDF and a CSV retention matrix. If you need explicit language for the SIG form, below is a suggested text snippet you can paste into Section C: 

"Redwood Inference retains request/response payloads in hosted environments for 30 days by default for operational troubleshooting. Customer content is not used for training unless explicitly authorized in contract. Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments may configure retention and opt-out options to eliminate storage of raw prompts and responses. Backups and long-term archives do not contain raw prompt/response payloads by default. Access to operational traces is strictly role-based and logged"

Please tell us which rows in Section C you want us to populate directly, and we'll send a redlined reply or hop on a call.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product — Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

(attachments: redwood_sig_evidence_log_handling_v1.pdf, redwood_data_retention_matrix.csv)

Karthik / Monica — thanks for the clear summary. A couple of follow-ups: 
1) For the "no-logging" flag on Hosted accounts, does that also suppress storage of prompt-derived metadata (token counts, request latency) used for billing and throttling? We need billing to remain accurate but prefer not to keep payloads.
2) For Dedicated customers who choose zero retention, can you confirm whether any temporary worker nodes or caches may leak prompt content into ephemeral disk (e.g., swap, local scratch) and whether those are part of standard disk-wipe policies?
3) We also need a short attestation that backups/snapshots do not contain prompt content because our auditors are checking S3 snapshot policies.

Can you provide answers in writing so we can include them as exhibits? If you prefer, we can mark the rows as "needs vendor attestation" and bring this to our SOC review.

Thanks,
Baldwin Procurement Team

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SIG Section C - clarifications on prompt logs and training usage

Hi Sarah / Baldwin procurement — adding the technical clarifications you requested and an attestation paragraph you can paste into the SIG.

Answers: 
1) "No-logging" behavior: The tenant-level no-logging flag prevents retention of full request/response payloads. Minimal operational metadata required for billing (request timestamp, token count, route id) is retained in an aggregated, non-payload form to support accurate billing and quota enforcement. Token counts are collected as numeric metadata only; they are never stored alongside raw prompt text when no-logging is enabled.

2) Ephemeral storage / worker nodes: For Hosted and Dedicated services we run ephemeral inference workers that may have request-derived data in memory and short-lived local caches. Those workers do not persist payloads to durable disk by default; local ephemeral storage is wiped on container shutdown and host reprovisioning. For Dedicated customers who choose zero retention, we enforce stricter disk-wipe and quarantine policies and can provide standard wipe logs on request as part of onboarding.

3) Backups and snapshots attestation (for SIG): 
"Attestation: Redwood Inference confirms that persistent backups and long-term snapshots of control-plane storage do not contain customer prompt or model response payloads. Operational traces that temporarily include payloads are excluded from persistent backups by default; in cases where a troubleshooting snapshot is created it is time-limited, access-controlled, and removed after the incident window. Access is logged and auditable"

Evidence & links: I have uploaded a short evidence packet (redwood_sig_evidence_log_handling_v1.pdf) and the retention matrix. For auditors we can provide wipe logs and worker provisioning records under NDA / contract.

If you want, let's schedule a 20-minute call tomorrow to sign off on the exact wording for Section C. When would be good for you?

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
